GC.7.1.statement: Incident handling processes are organizational; RHEL provides auditd, the systemd journal, and documented integration paths for centralized logging when configured by the customer.

STM.5.1.statement: RHEL ships auditd and documents audit record configuration. Log forwarding to SIEM or log servers is customer-configured via rsyslog, systemd-journal-remote, or equivalent.

STM.5.2.statement: Time synchronization for audit correlation is typically provided by chrony; customers point strata to trusted time sources as documented for RHEL.

DET.3.1.1.statement: RHEL auditd can record authentication success and failure events when audit rules are configured per product documentation and scap-security-guide baselines.

DET.3.1.2.statement: RHEL provides configurable audit rules (including privileged command and syscall auditing) via auditd; rule sets are customer-selected. See security hardening and OpenSCAP content for examples.

DET.3.1.4.statement: RHEL records system errors through the systemd journal and audit subsystem; retention and central collection are customer-defined.

DET.3.3.statement: auditd supports disk-full actions and space-left thresholds documented for RHEL; partition sizing and archival remain customer responsibilities.

DET.3.4.statement: RHEL documents restrictive permissions on audit log files and optional immutable audit rules to reduce tampering; forwarding to a separate log host or SIEM is customer-configured.

BER.2.4.statement: Changes to identity-related files can be recorded with auditd rules; identity lifecycle and IAM processes remain customer-owned (PAM, SSSD, directory integration).
